sections.content:
94,080 people

were counted on the census as "farmers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Farmers and related occupations cultivate arable crops, fruits and trees, and raise cattle, sheep, pigs, poultry and other livestock for consumption.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "farmers" there were more men than women (80.8% compared with 19.2%).

This means "farmers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled agricultural and related trades".

Men made up 80.8% and women made up 19.2% of "farmers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "farmers" included:

  • managers in transport and distribution
  • IT operations technicians
  • managers in storage and warehousing

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "farmers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "farmers", 29% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "farmers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "farmers" included:

  • managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture
  • elected officers and representatives
  • typists and related keyboard occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "farmers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "farmers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "farmers", 12.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (83.7% compared with 16.3%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (83.1%) than an employee (16.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Powys, this is in Wales.
